findings.title: Concurrent GET can discard an original ACK and adopt apparent writer authority before that command completes
findings.cause: callV2 captures pending at line66, increments a shared presentation ticket at88–89, then returns STALE_RESPONSE at98 before recording ACK at99–102. A later GET started while the original command is in flight has pending=null and a newer ticket; it can adopt a snapshot at109–114 while the original ACK was discarded. The transport serializes HTTP, not command lifecycle state admission.
findings.impact: A fully valid ACK may lose the original command replay/completion barrier. A schema-valid GET writer snapshot can then enable another write even though the original attach/write never completed.
findings.existing_coverage_gap: Current pending-takeover controls await the first ACK before GET. The late/atomic tuple tests do not place the newer GET between issuance of A and processing its ACK.
required_change: Maintain command-in-flight/pending identity independently of presentation/read tickets; reserve or serialize command admission before asynchronous exposure.
Validated ACK must preserve the exact original command/request barrier even when a newer read presentation is pending; never clear it based on GET.
At authority adoption commit, consult current command state rather than a stale captured pending variable. Only a validated terminal response for the original command may release its barrier.
Retain tuple/context generation protections: no stale command completion may mutate a newly selected project/session, and no blind resubmission/new command_id is allowed.
findings.minimal_bounds: Original ipc.js callV259–110 (current59–119) is already owned. Function-local state or a callV2-owned WeakMap can stay inside that function. Keep original protected1–8,11–58,163–191 byte exact; no first11/export/native/browser edits needed.

findings.title: Private protocol accepts non-exact packet members/types and non-JSON framing whitespace
findings.cause: Go struct decoding is case-insensitive even with DisallowUnknownFields; the subsequent map checks only member count. A six-member packet using Schema instead of schema is accepted; null response_raw_base64 becomes the zero string and satisfies REQUEST. In the reverse direction privateJSON uses JavaScript /\s/, admitting NBSP and other whitespace outside JSON grammar.
findings.impact: The declared strict six-key/type and single valid JSON packet boundary is weaker than its frozen private protocol. The normal producer emits valid bytes, but malformed private stream controls must fail closed rather than silently normalize.
required_change: Before struct projection, validate exact decoded key set and each raw JSON type. Five fields are non-null strings; http_status is null only for REQUEST or an integer in100..599 for RESPONSE. Keep strict duplicate/Unicode/base64/phase and raw byte limits.
Limit privateJSON insignificant whitespace to U+0020,U+0009,U+000A,U+000D. Keep duplicate decoded keys, invalid Unicode, unsafe numbers, trailing values, size and depth refusals.
Add fixed-byte negative controls without modifying frozen public schemas or relaxing existing 159+7 predicates.
